Container image runs on managed VM; not full root/nested virtualization sandbox.

Unknowns remain null, not free; Docker-app regime is an ordinary self-serve PaaS instance (not alt).

VAT basis: Unknown: reviewed pricing source does not explicitly establish VAT/tax inclusion.
Residency: Normalized Paris (par); zone catalog includes other deployments, so EU-only residency requires pinning Paris and storage.
clever.cloud/pricing (2026-09-28): self-serve pay-as-you-go, "billed by the second". Size/price table comes from the public price-system API (sources).

Clever Tasks: a Docker app can run as a run-to-completion job ('Clever Cloud just starts a VM, run the given command and then stop the VM'), billed per second at the same flavor price; no inbound HTTP/TCP.
Monthly prepaid provisioning: each month's invoice includes a top-up of prepaid credits equal to estimated next-month consumption (not a minimum fee).
nano (and pico) instances run with reduced CPU priority on the host and may slow down when the hypervisor is loaded; no baseline is published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Clever Cloud instances are to be seen as *read-only* resources. Any change made on an instance **will not be persisted**.
snapshot_auto.note: Immutable-infrastructure PaaS: every deploy/restart creates a new VM from the build (a build cache archive is reused, not machine state). Persistence is via add-ons (FS Bucket, Cellar S3, databases). FS Buckets get automated backups every 24 h (72 h retention), databases 7 days.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Immutable infrastructure doesn’t allow you to keep generated data files between deployments.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No instance snapshot/checkpoint API in docs, CLI reference or API v4 overview; add-on backups only.

harness_api.quote: Nothing here is an AI-specific product.
harness_api.note: Agents drive the platform from outside via Clever Tools CLI, the public API and the open-source mcp-simple-server; SSH exec into instances is suggested for Claude Code/Codex/Cursor/OpenCode diagnostics. No API to run/stream an agent harness inside an app.

ingress_rules.quote: OAuth2 Proxy redirects unauthenticated visitors to the identity provider you configure, and only authenticated requests reach your application.
ingress_rules.note: Controls: only HTTP port 8080 is exposed by default; raw TCP only via opt-in TCP redirections (port 4040 -> random public port); Network Groups (WireGuard private network between apps/add-ons/external peers, beta) for private access; platform-managed OAuth2 Proxy / Otoroshi challenge in the request flow; dedicated load balancers with fixed inbound IPs (quote-based). No documented IP allowlist or security-group style inbound rules; the HTTP endpoint itself is always public.

volume_attach.quote: This is why we created File System Buckets, a network-based storage solution to retrieve data from a deployment to another.
volume_attach.note: FS Bucket add-on, mounted via CC_FS_BUCKET env var (several buckets per app, optional :async). Network FS, not block volumes. NOT available for Docker applications ('FS Buckets access ... not supported' on the Docker page), not in the HDS zone, not cross-region.

volume_shared.quote: Since the folder is mounted over the network, multiple instances/applications can read it like any file on the system. At the same time.
volume_shared.note: Read-write, shared across instances and applications in the same region; docs warn concurrent writers can corrupt files. Not for Docker apps.

nested_virt.quote: Clever Cloud instances are to be seen as *read-only* resources... bas@67fbf787-3518-47bb-abd9-2c2575844edd ~ $
nested_virt.note: SSH access is to a non-root user ('bas') on an immutable instance; no docs mention /dev/kvm, privileged mode, or nested virtualization for Docker/runtime apps.

egress_ip_type.quote: EUR 490/month licence + 1.8x monthly consumption, 12-month commitment, 99.99% SLA, fixed outbound IP, 24/7 phone support
egress_ip_type.note: Standard pay-as-you-go apps share pooled datacenter outbound IPs (static_egress_ip=false in card); only the Premium commit plan adds a fixed outbound IP, so the base offering's egress IP type is shared/datacenter.

snapshot.quote: Clever Cloud instances are to be seen as *read-only* resources. Any change made on an instance **will not be persisted**.
snapshot.note: Immutable infrastructure: no instance filesystem or memory snapshot/checkpoint API; only add-ons (databases, FS Buckets) have their own backup systems.

fork.quote: Deploy applications on Clever Cloud with support for popular languages, frameworks, and deployment configurations across modern runtimes
fork.note: No documented API/CLI to clone a running or stopped instance into a new machine; new instances are always created fresh from a deploy/build.

fork_running.quote: Clever Cloud instances are to be seen as *read-only* resources. Any change made on an instance **will not be persisted**.
fork_running.note: not offered: no fork feature exists at all (see fork).

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Clever Cloud instances are to be seen as *read-only* resources. Any change made on an instance **will not be persisted**.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: no fork/snapshot feature exists at all.

pause_resume.quote: The calculation of consumption is based on the second of running.
pause_resume.note: Apps/scalers can be stopped and restarted via Console/CLI; billing is by the second of running, so a stopped app is not billed while stopped.

wake_on_request.quote: When enabling auto-scalability, you have to set a minimum and a maximum of active scalers in your apps settings.
wake_on_request.note: Auto-scaling reacts to load on already-running scalers; no documented feature that wakes a fully stopped application automatically when an inbound request arrives.

auto_stop_idle.quote: When enabling auto-scalability, you have to set a minimum and a maximum of active scalers in your apps settings.
auto_stop_idle.note: Auto-scaling documentation covers scaling instance count/size with load, not automatically stopping an idle app to zero; Clever Tasks (run-to-completion jobs) is the closest analog but is a different product mode.

live_resize.quote: Clever Cloud instances are to be seen as *read-only* resources. Any change made on an instance **will not be persisted**.
live_resize.note: Immutable-infrastructure model: changing a scaler flavor (vCPU/RAM) redeploys/recreates instances rather than resizing a running one in place; no documented in-place live resize API.

agent_harnesses.quote: Nothing here is an AI-specific product.
agent_harnesses.note: No coding-agent (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode) template or preinstalled harness; agents are expected to drive the platform externally via CLI/API/MCP.

own_agent_api.quote: Nothing here is an AI-specific product.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Clever Cloud has no first-party browser/computer-use/research agent product.

mcp_server.quote: [`mcp-simple-server`](https://github.com/CleverCloud/mcp-simple-server) | Agents speaking the Model Context Protocol
mcp_server.note: First-party MCP server exposing search/execute/doc tools against the Clever Cloud API.

lang_python.note: Python is a first-class supported application runtime.

lang_node.quote: Currently, Clever Cloud supports: ... - Node.js & Bun
lang_node.note: Node.js (& Bun) is a first-class supported application runtime.

public_ipv4.quote: Request load balancers dedicated to your organisation for isolated capacity, fixed inbound IP addresses and redundancy
public_ipv4.note: Apps are reached through Clever Cloud's shared reverse-proxy/load-balancer layer (domains/HTTPS), not a public IPv4 assigned per machine; a per-organisation fixed/dedicated IP is a separate paid add-on for the routing layer, not a plain per-instance IPv4.

egress_allowlist.quote: Network Groups (NG) are a way to create a private secure network between resources inside Clever Cloud infrastructure, using WireGuard.
egress_allowlist.note: Network Groups provide private mesh networking between selected resources, not a general outbound allow/deny-list or no-internet mode for arbitrary internet egress; no such control documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: When a resource is linked to a Network Group, you can reach it on any port inside this private network with its domain name.
egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP method/path-level egress rule mechanism documented; Network Groups only govern private inter-resource connectivity.

guest_firewall.note: SSH sessions run as a non-root user ('bas') on read-only, immutable instances; no documented root/sudo access, so guest-side nftables/iptables configuration is not expected to work.

secret_proxy.quote: creates them, links them, and reads the injected credentials from the environment
secret_proxy.note: Add-on credentials (databases, object storage, etc.) are injected as environment variables into the instance; no first-party proxy that injects credentials into outbound HTTP calls without the secret entering the machine.

gpu.quote: nano, XS, S, M, L, XL, 2XL, 3XL
gpu.note: not offered: the published instance sizes and product catalog (llms.txt) list no GPU flavor or GPU add-on.

windows.quote: Currently, Clever Cloud supports: .NET, Docker, Elixir, Go, Haskell, Java ... Linux, Meteor.js, Node.js & Bun, PHP and FrankenPHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Static sites, V
windows.note: not offered: all listed application runtimes run on Linux instances; Windows only appears as a client OS for installing the Clever Tools CLI, not as a machine OS.

macos.quote: Currently, Clever Cloud supports: .NET, Docker, Elixir, Go, Haskell, Java ... Linux, Meteor.js, Node.js & Bun, PHP and FrankenPHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Static sites, V
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no macOS machine type in the runtime/product catalog.

arm64.quote: nano, XS, S, M, L, XL, 2XL, 3XL
arm64.note: No ARM instance flavor documented in pricing/product pages or the changelog; scaler catalog and changelog (kernel/runtime updates) show no ARM-specific offering.

self_host.quote: Discover our Clever Cloud On-Premises offer and add automation on your own on-premises infrastructure.
self_host.note: "Clever Cloud On-Premises" packages the platform for private data centers, available since 2016 upon request (sales@clever-cloud.com).

open_source.note: Tooling (Clever Tools CLI, client libraries, mcp-simple-server, documentation) is open source, but the core hosting platform itself is a closed, proprietary PaaS - not released under an OSI license.

soc2.quote: Our certifications ISO 27001 : 2022 HDS Health Data Hosting SecNumCloud
soc2.note: The Security/certifications page lists ISO 27001, HDS and SecNumCloud (French sovereign-cloud qualification) but no SOC 2 attestation.

hipaa.quote: Health Data Hosting ... In accordance with requirements 29 and 30 of the HDS framework
hipaa.note: not offered: Clever Cloud's healthcare-data compliance is the French HDS (Hébergeur de Données de Santé) framework, not the US HIPAA/BAA regime — outside the product's (EU-based) regulatory scope.

sso.quote: Team members must have a Clever Cloud account.
sso.note: Organisation/member management docs describe adding team members who each need an individual Clever Cloud account; no SAML/OIDC single sign-on integration is documented.

eu_data_residency.quote: Applications and add-ons are deployed in multiple regions across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific, including Paris, Roubaix, Gravelines, London, Warsaw ... plus HDS-certified zones in France for healthcare data.
eu_data_residency.note: Multiple EU zones (Paris, Roubaix, Gravelines, London, Warsaw) let customers pin deployment to the EU; company itself is based in Nantes, France.

max_session_h.quote: The calculation of consumption is based on the second of running.
max_session_h.note: Applications/scalers are long-running services billed per second with no documented maximum session/runtime limit; they run until stopped or redeployed (Clever Tasks run-to-completion jobs are a separate, different mode).

persistent_disk.quote: Clever Cloud instances are to be seen as *read-only* resources. Any change made on an instance **will not be persisted**. ... Changes made on instances are not kept across deployments.
persistent_disk.note: Immutable-infrastructure PaaS: no root-disk persistence, no pause/resume of app instances, and no instance snapshot/checkpoint API (confirmed separately for snapshot_auto/snapshot_on_demand: 'Immutable infrastructure doesn't allow you to keep generated data files between deployments'). Auto/vertical/horizontal scaling docs describe replacing instances, not pausing them with retained disk. The only first-party persistence mechanisms are network-attached add-ons (FS Bucket, databases, Cellar S3) which are separate resources, not the instance's own disk -- already captured via volume_attach/volume_shared=true. No contradiction found: card has pause_resume=null, snapshot_auto=false, volumes=null, all consistent with 'no persistent disk'.

static_egress_ip.note: Feature-comparison table: standard Clever Cloud plan has no fixed outbound IP, but the paid Premium plan (€490/month + 1.8x consumption, 12-month commitment) includes a 'Unified Gateway' delivering a fixed/unique outbound IP. So static_egress_ip should be true (opt-in, Premium-plan-only), not false as currently recorded with no evidence.

byoc.quote: Discover our Clever Cloud On-Premises offer and add automation on your own on-premises infrastructure. ... Applications and databases are running on your servers. ... An existing hardware infrastructure (servers, network, storage) and operational teams ready to collaborate with Clever Cloud.
byoc.note: Clever Cloud's only 'run it on infrastructure you control' offer is 'Clever Cloud On-Premises', which is installed on the customer's own physical hardware/datacenter (self_host), not a Clever-Cloud-managed deployment into the customer's own AWS/GCP/Azure cloud account. No BYOC-into-your-cloud-account product is documented.
